title: Draining a gum abscess
what: The doctor makes a small cut in the gum and lets the pus out. This relieves the pressure and pain.
why: When a bad tooth causes swelling of the gum and cheek, pain, and pus.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes
tell_doctor: If you are allergic to numbing medicine or other medicines
If you have diabetes or heart disease
When the swelling started and if you had a fever

prepare.title: No heat
prepare.text: Do not put anything warm on your cheek. It can make the infection worse.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can eat beforehand. For a couple of hours after the procedure, your mouth will still be numb.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your medicines on your own. Tell the doctor everything you take.

bring: Past X-rays of the tooth, if you have them
steps: The doctor checks the tooth and gum, often with an X-ray
The doctor makes a small cut in the gum
The pus is let out and the area is rinsed
Sometimes a thin rubber strip is left in to help it drain
The doctor decides what to do with the tooth: treat it now or later
feel: The numbing injection is a quick sting
During the cut, you feel pressure but not pain
When the numbness wears off, it may ache for 1 to 3 days, usually less than before
after: Rinse and take medicines exactly as the doctor said
Do not warm your cheek, and do not touch the wound with your tongue
You usually come back in 1 to 2 days, and the strip is removed
The tooth that caused it must be treated or removed. The doctor will tell you
red_flags: The swelling grows and spreads to your neck or under your eye: call emergency services
It is hard to swallow, breathe, or open your mouth: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C that stays or goes up
New pus and severe pain after 2 to 3 days

faq.q: Can I treat an abscess at home?
faq.a: No. The pus needs to be let out and the tooth treated. Pills alone do not fix the problem.

faq.q: Why can't I warm my cheek?
faq.a: Heat can make the infection worse and spread the pus.

reminders.text: Abscess visit soon. Do not warm your cheek. Bring your list of medicines.
